inputs.name: jenkins_version
inputs.description: Jenkins LTS release to install, such as "2.580.2". Raising it upgrades Jenkins in place.

inputs.name: java_version
inputs.description: OpenJDK release to run Jenkins on, from the distribution's packages: 21 or 25, the two Jenkins supports. Fedora 45 packages only 25.

inputs.name: plugin_manager_version
inputs.description: Release of Jenkins' plugin installation manager tool, which installs the plugins. Change plugin_manager_sha256 with it.

inputs.name: plugin_manager_sha256
inputs.description: SHA-256 of jenkins-plugin-manager-VERSION.jar. Change it with plugin_manager_version.

inputs.name: plugins
inputs.description: Plugins to install, by ID, with the version of each, such as { timestamper = "1.30", git = "latest" }. configuration-as-code is always installed; list it to pick its version.

inputs.name: plugins_file
inputs.description: Local path of a plugins.txt, one ID:VERSION per line, installed as well as plugins. When null, none.

inputs.name: admin_username
inputs.description: ID of the Jenkins user JCasC creates with admin_password.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password of admin_username, set by JCasC on every start of Jenkins. Pass it at run time with -var or TF_VAR_admin_password; it never reaches state or the plan.

inputs.name: casc
inputs.description: More Jenkins Configuration as Code, as an object written to casc.yaml, such as { jenkins = { numExecutors = 0 } }. The circuit sets jenkins.securityRealm and jenkins.authorizationStrategy itself, and unclassified.location.url when url is set.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: Address people reach Jenkins by, such as "https://ci.example.com/". Jenkins builds the links in its emails and build statuses from it. When null, Jenkins leaves it empty and warns about it.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Address Jenkins listens on. The default keeps it to the host itself, for a proxy in front; "0.0.0.0" listens on every address.

inputs.name: heap_size
inputs.description: JVM heap, set as both -Xms and -Xmx, such as "1g". When null, Java sizes it at a quarter of the host's memory.
